title: QUIZ - 98
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the truth value of the negation of a statement with known truth value
questions.question: The statement "A square has four equal sides." is true. What is the truth value of its negation (NOT the statement)?
questions.explanation: Negation always reverses the truth value. Since the original statement is true, its negation is false.
questions.hint: Negation (NOT) always flips a statement's truth value: true becomes false, and false becomes true.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize that applying negation twice returns the original truth value
questions.question: The statement "The number 3 is an even number." is false. What is the truth value of NOT(NOT(the statement)) — the negation applied twice?

options.label: A
options.text: It depends on which negation is applied first

questions.explanation: Applying negation twice returns the original truth value: NOT(NOT(p)) is logically equivalent to p. Since the statement is false, double negation gives false.
questions.hint: Negating a statement twice always returns you to its original truth value.

questions.concept: Writing the Negation of a Statement
questions.learningObjective: Construct the correct logical negation of a given statement
questions.question: What is the correct logical negation of the statement: "The store is open."?

options.label: B
options.text: The store is open. and something else is also true.

questions.explanation: The strict logical negation of "The store is open." is "The store is not open." — simply asserting the statement is not the case, without assuming any particular alternative.
questions.hint: The logical negation of a statement simply asserts that the statement is not true; it should not assume a specific opposite condition.
